title: GPU image cohortization and release orchestrator for driver/stack compatibility
creator: Liam Park
description:
Problem: We currently struggle to coordinate safe upgrades across container images, OS packages, SBOMs, and pinned CUDA/driver stacks. Ad-hoc canaries have surfaced hardware-driver mismatches in the field and forced emergency rollbacks. This ticket scopes a reusable release orchestration layer that: 1) groups images into cohorts based on identical kernel/driver/ABI footprints (cohortization), 2) emits an artifact manifest (image bundle + SBOM + driver pin list + validation checksum), 3) drives staged rollouts with programmable gates (health, driver-mismatch rate, tail-latency degradation), and 4) integrates with existing LTS channels to make upgrades explicit for customers on stable tiers.

Goals: Establish an automated pipeline that produces a canonical "release bundle" per rollout and runs an acceptance matrix across representative hardware fleets before promoting to LTS. Provide clear rollback and mitigation actions that can be triggered automatically or by on-call.

Non-goals: This ticket does not rework the kernel packaging process or replace OS-level driver installers; it coordinates artifacts and validation at the release orchestration layer.

Success metrics: reduction in post-rollout driver-related SEVs by 90% for the pilot fleet; average time-to-rollback < 8 minutes for automated rollbacks; ability to produce a bundle manifest and SBOM delta within 3 minutes of image build completion.

Design overview: The orchestrator will:
- Consume build outputs (image digest, signed SBOM, driver pin metadata) and assemble a JSON manifest with explicit compatibility fingerprints.
- Compute cohort keys by hashing (image digest, kernel ABI tag, driver-version, runtime flags) to group images likely to share runtime compatibility.
- Launch staged canaries: small cohort on a canary pool -> progressive gating to larger cohorts and finally LTS promotion.
- Evaluate gates via a rule engine: latency SLA, error rate, driver mismatch telemetry (device init failures), memory reclamation anomalies.
- Provide an API for Console to display cohort status, gate logs, and allow manual override with audit trails.

Trade-offs considered: Maintaining many cohorts increases coverage but multiplies release overhead and storage for SBOM snapshots. We favor coarse cohorts for GA channels and finer cohorts for dedicated/private customers with strict hardware matrices. We will limit the pilot to 3 cohort granularities (coarse/medium/fine) and iterate.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline emits a signed release bundle manifest (image digest + SBOM + driver pin list) for every release candidate
Cohortization algorithm produces deterministic grouping for a given build hash and hardware matrix
Automated gate runner can evaluate at least 4 metric predicates and decide promote/rollback
Canary rollback is triggered automatically when driver-mismatch-rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes
Console shows cohort and gate state with links to artifacts and audit log entries
Documentation (Confluence) describes rollback runbook and LTS promotion checklist
technical_notes: Validation matrix will run on the existing CI hardware lab (lab-1, lab-2) using runtime-1.20 docker images
SBOM delta step: use existing sbom-diff tool to surface file-level package changes and highlight new kernel module packages
Driver ABI validator will call a lightweight probe that attempts to load libcuda and run a small kernel on a pinned driver inside a sandboxed container
Manifest format proposal: release_bundle:v1 => {bundle_id, cohort_key, images:[{name,digest}], sbom_url, driver_pin_list, checksums, signed_by}
Retention policy: keep signed bundle manifests and SBOMs for 180 days for LTS channels and 30 days for ephemeral dev channels
